title: Reserve Transfer Protocol and Graceful Preemption (RTP) for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Define and deliver a Reserve Transfer Protocol (RTP) and accompanying graceful preemption mechanics to allow controlled transfers of reserved capacity between tenants/pools and safe preemption of ephemeral workloads, minimizing customer impact and providing auditability.
problem_statement: Customers with reserved GPU pools sometimes need to reassign headroom between tenants or accept short-term overcommit bursts while protecting high-priority workload SLAs. Today, reassigning reserved capacity is manual and risky; preemption is abrupt and causes increased latency and errors. We need a protocol and controls that enable safe transfers and gentle preemption with observable guarantees and rollback.
goals: Design an RTP API and control-plane flow that supports dry-run, approve, and execute modes for moving reserved capacity between pools or tenants.
Implement graceful preemption semantics that drain in-flight requests, respect per-tenant grace windows, and optionally migrate work to fallback model variants or hosted tiers.
Expose audit logs and immutable transfer records for compliance and billing reconciliation.
Integrate RTP with existing autoscale governor so transfers and preemptions are policy-driven (priority, cost center, SLA tiers).
Provide telemetry and console surface (transfer history, pending transfers, preemption events, impact windows) to SRE/Customer Success.
success_metrics: Reduce customer-reported P1 preemption incidents by 60% within 3 months of rollout.
Average error-rate spike from preemption events <= 1.5x baseline for affected tenants.
90% of transfers complete without manual intervention (approve/execute via API/console).
Auditable transfer record exists for 100% of capacity moves with a unique transfer ID and timestamps.
Rollout telemetry shows <5% of transfers requiring rollback during Canary.
No degradation to global latency SLOs for non-impacted tenants during transfer windows.
Console adoption: 25 customers use RTP features for planned reassignments within 60 days.
non_goals: Replace long-term capacity contract negotiation workflows (this is operational reassignments and emergency headroom, not billing contract changes).
Full cross-cloud, cross-region live migration of running containers/VMs (we manage inference-level drain and rerouting only).
Support for arbitrary third-party schedulers to directly control RTP (we will provide API hooks and webhooks only).
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want to move 4 reserved GPUs from tenant A to tenant B for 2 hours to support a high-priority demo, so the demo meets latency targets without disrupting tenant A beyond a defined grace window.
As an SRE, I want a dry-run mode to simulate a transfer's effect on headroom and predicted preemption, so I can approve or adjust policy before execution.
As a customer success engineer, I want a clear audit trail and reason codes for every transfer so billing reconciliation and customer communications are straightforward.
As a tenant admin, I want an opt-in soft-quarantine mode which applies a short TTL to low-priority requests during transfer windows instead of abrupt evictions.
As a product owner, I want RTP integrated with autoscale policies so transfers can be triggered automatically when predictive indicators show sustained headroom imbalance.
As an auditor, I want immutable transfer records and signed webhook events so compliance teams can verify actions post-facto.
requirements: Control plane API: POST /transfers with payload (source_pool, dest_pool, gpus, start_time, duration, mode={dry-run|approve|execute}, reason, approver_id).
Transfer lifecycle states: pending, simulated, approved, executing, draining, committed, rolled_back, failed. State changes must emit events to webhook subscriptions and console notifications.

Graceful preemption: when executing, affected nodes enter DRAINING state with a configurable drain_window (default 60s) during which new low-priority requests are queued or redirected and in-flight tokens are allowed to complete.

Soft-quarantine mode: requests below tenant-specified priority get a short TTL (configurable 15-120s) rather than immediate eviction; if TTL expires, request is failed with a clear preemption error code.
Fallback routing: if configured, the runtime should automatically route preempted requests to a compatible hosted model variant with a cost/latency warning returned to the caller.
Transfer ledger: every transfer must create an immutable record with transfer_id, signature (HMAC), initiator, approver, timestamps, resources moved, pre/post capacity snapshots, and reason_code.
Autoscale governor hooks: RTP must expose signals (pending_transfer, transfer_impact_estimate, shortfall_prediction) to the governor so policy rules can auto-schedule transfers.
RBAC and approvals: UI/API flows must enforce approver roles (owner, platform-admin) and support delegated approvals via policy (e.g., auto-approve below threshold X).

Telemetry: emit metrics: transfers_started, transfers_committed, transfers_rolledback, preemption_events, preemption_error_rate_by_tenant, drain_completion_time, fallback_routed_count. Metrics must be available in console dashboards and exported to Prometheus.

Runbook and rollbacks: provide an API endpoint to abort running transfers and a console button to initiate rollback; rollback must restore previous capacity allocation within the specified recovery_window.
Backwards compatibility: existing reserved-pool APIs must continue to work; RTP is additive and can be disabled per-organization.
Compliance: transfer ledger retained for at least 365 days and available for export; webhook signatures and audit routes must meet SOC2 logging expectations.
acceptance_criteria: API contract validated: unit and contract tests for /transfers and lifecycle transitions; documented OpenAPI schema checked into repo.
End-to-end integration tests simulate dry-run -> approve -> execute flows and assert capacity snapshots and telemetry emission.
Graceful preemption verification: simulated workloads show in-flight requests complete within drain_window and low-priority requests receive TTL-based failures instead of immediate evictions.
Fallback routing works for at least two model families and returns documented response flags and metrics; fallback count surfaces in console.
Auditability: transfer ledger entries include HMAC signature; exporting ledger yields CSV with expected fields and timestamps.
Governor integration: autoscale policy rule can trigger a transfer in staging; transfer events are received by the governor and visible in console.
Console UX: transfer creation, pending approvals, progress, and history pages are implemented and pass accessibility review.
Rollout safety: canary rollout to 5 pilot customers shows rollback rate <5% and acceptable impact on their SLAs; SRE runbook updated with playbook steps.
Performance: RTP control-plane adds <5% p90 latency to reserved-pool list/write operations under normal load.
Security: RBAC checks enforced in API; webhook signatures verified; security review completed with mitigation notes addressed.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: API + simulation + internal e2e tests (2 weeks). Phase 2: Implement runtime draining semantics and soft-quarantine (3 weeks). Phase 3: Integrate with autoscale governor + telemetry + console surfaces (3 weeks). Phase 4: Canary with 5 pilot customers for 4 weeks; gather metrics and iterate. Phase 5: Gradual ramp to all customers by policy opt-in, followed by on-by-default after 90 days if metrics stable.
dependencies: Autoscale governor hooks and signal schema (ENG-46780)
Console: new transfer UI and history pages (DES-12899)
Telemetry: add transfer metrics to ingestion pipeline (ENG-44500)
Security: audit of HMAC signing and retention policy (SEC-9901)
open_questions: What are safe default thresholds for auto-approval across tenant tiers? (suggestion: <4 GPUs & <2h auto-approve for Standard tier).
Should fallback routing incur automatic billing adjustments, or just warn customers?
How should transfer cost attribution be reflected on invoices when transfers cross billing units?
Do we need a hard cap on number of concurrent transfers per region to protect control-plane availability?
What's the desired retention for transfer telemetry beyond audit ledger (30d vs 90d)?
notes: Prototype dry-run implementation in staging reduced failed preemptions during maintenance by 70% in a 3-day experiment.
Design suggested a 'gentle eviction' code to be returned by runtime so SDKs can surface user-friendly messages and recommended retry windows.
We will present RTP at the next SRE weekly for feedback on recovery_window defaults and throttling policies.
